name: Art Practice (BA)

rules.name: Overview
rules.desc: The Art Practice major coursework includes six lower-level studio courses, six upper-level studio courses, and four art history/critical theory courses. Students explore different media and build an understanding of the scope of contemporary art practice in the lower-level courses, including the core studio Foundation series, ARTSTUDI 101 and ARTSTUDI 102. In addition to ARTSTUDI201 - Art Practice Major Seminar and ARTSTUDI 249 - Art Practice Capstone, students focus their practice through upper-level electives in specific areas of interest; the courses are designed to deepen the students' knowledge of particular materials and techniques and stretch their understanding of conceptual issues.

children.name: Foundation and History
children.notes: Art Practice Foundation courses, ARTSTUDI101 and ARTSTUDI102, can be completed in any order.

children.name: Lower-Level Electives
children.desc:
Any 100-level ARTSTUDI course may be applied toward the lower-level Art Practice elective requirement. Current course offerings can be found on Navigate Classes.
Students must complete a total of 16 units of lower-level ARTSTUDI courses.
children.notes:
Two 2-unit MFA-taught ARTSTUDI courses may be combined to satisfy one lower-level Art Practice elective.
Completing a full year of ITALIC can count as 4 units towards either one lower 100-level Art Practice elective or one Art History elective.

children.name: Upper-Level Electives
children.desc:
Any 200-level ARTSTUDI course may be applied toward the upper-level Art Practice elective requirement. Current course offerings can be found on Navigate Classes.
Students must complete a total of 16 units of upper-level ARTSTUDI courses.
children.notes:
Up to 4 units of the honors coursework (ARTSTUDI 297 and ARTSTUDI 297S) may count towards one upper-level elective.
Independent study, which a faculty member supervises, is also available on a case-by-case basis as a component of a student’s 200-level coursework for the degree. For Independent Study to apply to the major, it must be taken for four units.

children.name: Art History Electives
children.desc: Majors must complete three additional art history/critical theory elective courses. Any ARTHIST course may be applied toward the Art History elective requirement. One Film & Media Studies (FILMEDIA) course may satisfy an art history/critical theory elective. Current course offerings can be found on Navigate Classes.
children.notes:
One of these electives may be fulfilled by a course offered by another department with advisor approval. Substitute courses should emphasize critical analysis and interpretation of art and/or film, engagement with primary and secondary sources, and the study of artistic movements, theory, or sociohistorical contexts.
Completing a full year of ITALIC can count as 4 units towards either one lower 100-level Art Practice elective or one Art History elective.

rules.name: Required Course
rules.notes: ARTSTUDI 201 should be taken during junior year.

rules.name: Overview and Requirements
rules.desc:
The Department of Art & Art History’s year-long Honors Program allows selected Art Practice majors to develop a self-initiated body of thesis artwork throughout their senior year in parallel with their regular work for the Art Practice major. The body of thesis artwork students propose and develop is expected to deepen and elaborate on work and themes they have begun to explore in previous courses or independent work. This thesis artwork is exhibited in an honors exhibition in the early Spring of the senior year. Students also produce a written thesis paper contextualizing and documenting this work.
The Honors Program is open to Art Practice majors in their senior year who are studying on campus for the entire year. Admission to the Honors Program is decided by the Art Practice faculty via a competitive application process in Spring of the junior year. Completion of the Honors Program is noted on the student’s diploma and transcript.
Participation in the Honors Program requires 10 units of honors-specific coursework dedicated to producing the thesis artwork, exhibition, and written thesis. Up to 4 units of this honors coursework may count towards one of the four upper-level elective courses required for the major. The Honors Program requires a minimum of 71 total credits, an additional 6 units beyond the 65-unit requirement for the Art Practice major.
While Art Practice honors students are expected to work independently to develop artwork for the thesis exhibition, they are supported via ongoing one-on-one tutorials with a faculty thesis mentor (which comprise 3 of the required 10 honors units) and via a year-long honors seminar with other honors students and the Director of the Honors Program (which comprise the remaining 7 required units). In the seminar, students engage with their honors cohort through critiques, visiting artists meetings, and other activities determined by the Honors Director.
During the Honors Program, to support honors students in producing their thesis work, students are typically given access to studio space in a shared honors studio, a materials stipend, and ongoing access to McMurtry Building area-specific studios (photography, sculpture, digital media, printmaking, painting) for which they have received training.
Admission to the Honors Program
To be eligible to apply for honors:

• Students must be in residence on campus all of their senior year.

• Students must have completed ARTSTUDI 101 - Foundations I, ARTSTUDI 102 - Foundations II, ARTHIST 5 - Art & Power, and at least five Art Practice classes by the end of junior year.

• Four must be completed by the end of Winter Quarter junior year when the honors application is submitted.
Detailed instructions for applying to the Honors Program during the Spring Quarter of junior year are listed on the Department of Art & Art History’s website.
Early in their junior year, students considering honors should contact Student Services to review the requirements and express interest in the program so that they will be notified of that year’s specific application deadlines and submission process.
The application includes a portfolio, project proposal, study plan, unofficial transcript, and signature of a full-time art practice faculty member who has advised the student on their honors application project proposal.
Students are selected for the Honors Program based on the strength of their application portfolio and project proposal. Students accepted into the Honors Program have illustrated their ability to work independently and rigorously on their artwork, participate productively in group critiques, and work respectfully in a shared studio space. The body of work students propose and develop for an honors exhibition is expected to deepen and elaborate on work and themes they have begun to explore in previous courses or independent work.
Honors Program Requirements
The Art Practice program requires students to develop a sustained studio practice across Fall and Winter Quarters in order to generate a body of thesis artwork approved by their Honors Faculty Mentor and the Honors Director. In the Spring Quarter, this body of thesis work must be successfully installed and exhibited in the thesis exhibition and documented and analyzed through the student’s written thesis document. Students must maintain an A- in all honors course components every quarter to achieve honors on the student’s transcript.
A minimum A- grade in both honors course components (ARTSTUDI 297, 297S) must be achieved each quarter to continue in honors each quarter.
Students must also pass a faculty review at the end of Fall Quarter with the Honors Director and their Faculty Mentor to continue in the Honors Program through Winter and Spring Quarters

• Artwork presented at the review must represent significant progress towards the student’s proposed thesis artwork.

• Students who do not pass this review will continue as regular Art Practice majors, but not as part of the Honors Program. In this case, credits obtained for the fall Honors Faculty Tutorial and Honors Seminar will count as regular elective credits towards the Art Practice major.
Continuing in honors past Winter Quarter is conditional upon the student’s body of thesis work being ready for the honors exhibition, as evaluated by the Honors Director, the student’s Faculty Mentor, and the Gallery Director.
During the Spring Quarter, students must successfully participate in the honors exhibition, with work approved by the Honors Director and their Faculty Mentor, and delivered and installed in a professional manner with the direction of the Gallery Director.
The written thesis, including multiple iterative drafts, must be successfully completed and submitted by the deadline set by the Honors Director in the Spring Quarter.

children.name: Tutorial Course
children.notes: Students must complete 3 units of ARTSTUDI 297 – AP Honors Tutorial (1 each quarter of senior year)

children.name: Honors Seminar
children.notes: Students must complete 7 units of ARTSTUDI 297S – AP Honors Seminar (3 in Fall, 2 in Winter, and 2 in Spring).

children.name: Fall faculty review with the Honors Director and Faculty Mentor

grading: All required and elective courses must be taken for a letter grade and must be passed with a letter grade of C or better.
policies:
During the first two weeks of each quarter, Art Practice majors must meet with their faculty advisor and the Student Services Specialist to have coursework approved and ensure they are meeting degree requirements.
Eligible students may also pursue a Bachelor of Arts in Art Practice with Honors.
Students are expected to pass reviews and critiques of their work throughout the quarter and participate in open studios and exhibitions as required by their art studio courses.
transferPolicy: Advanced placement test credit may not be applied toward any requirement of the major. A maximum of two courses (10 transfer units) from other universities and the Stanford Bing Overseas Studies Program may be applied to the 65 total units required for the major. Work from transfer courses must be evaluated by the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS) in Art Practice. Additional units must be petitioned to the Director of Undergraduate Studies in Art Practice and reviewed by a studio committee. Transfer credit may not be counted in any circumstance toward ARTSTUDI 201 - Major Seminar or ARTSTUDI 249 - Major Capstone.
otherRequirements: Interdisciplinary art survey, advanced undergraduate seminar, library orientation
reviewNotes: Every required and elective course must be taken for a letter grade with a C or better, toward the 65 units the major needs (71 with honors). The audit checks ARTSTUDI 101, 102 and ARTHIST 5, 16 units of 100-level ARTSTUDI courses, 16 units of 200-level ARTSTUDI courses other than the major seminar and capstone (up to 4 honors units may count there), three art history electives (any ARTHIST course, at most one FILMEDIA course), ARTSTUDI 201 and ARTSTUDI 249. You check by hand the library orientation, an outside art history course your advisor approves, at most two courses (10 units) taken away from Stanford, and for honors the A- in each honors course, the fall review, the exhibition and the written thesis.
